newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar official sees 1997/98 output dropping.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar official sees 1997/98 output dropping.

text.p: Thai Cane Sugar Board chief Pramote Vidtayasuk said on Monday that sugar output for the 1997/98 crop year could fall by 10 percent due to a lack of rainfall.
Pramote told Reuters he had received reports of cane plantations in many areas suffering from insufficient rain.
"Based on the situation, the sugar output could drop by around 10 percent from 1996/97 although some see a 15 percent fall," he said.
"That would bring the 1997/98 production to around 5.0-5.2 million tonnes from around 5.7 million tonnes (tel quel) this year," he said.
Only 20 percent of Thailand's sugar cane areas were irrigated, the rest depended entirely on rainfall.
"Some farmers started planting in March. Although there was some rainfall in April, that was far from being enough. In certain areas, their crops are dying," he said.
"Even though it would start raining soon, it would be a bit late for some areas where the crops are likely to give poor yields," he added.
Thailand's cane output for 1996/97 was around 56 million tonnes.
